newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais hold two Khmer Rouge guerrillas.
newsitem.headline: Thais hold two Khmer Rouge guerrillas.

text.p: Thai paratroopers on Wednesday detained two guerrillas from Cambodia's disintegrating Khmer Rouge rebel group as they crossed into Thailand carrying US$300,000, military sources said.
Notorious Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot has been captured by a splinter group of his Maoist movement that has turned against their ageing leader.
The guerrillas were held as they crossed into northeastern Si Sa Khet province in Thailand. The cash was taken from them, the sources said.
"I was informed that they (Thai soldiers) have arrested two senior Khmer Rouge guerrillas and confiscated about $300,000 but there are no further details available," one source said.
The source said that guerrillas who carried such large sums of money were believed to be high-ranking officers in the Khmer Rouge.
Ailing Khmer Rouge supremo Pol Pot, 69, is believed to be held hostage by his former comrades in the Khmer Rouge stronghold of Anlong Veng.

Cambodian authorities are seeking to bring him before an international tribunal for his "killing fields" rule of terror in Cambodia in the late 1970s when over a million people died of starvation, disease or overwork.
